text.en: Max is a small brown dog. He loves to play with a soft blue ball in the garden. Every afternoon, Max runs on the green grass. When he gets tired, he sleeps in a warm basket.
text.zh: 麦克斯是一只棕色的小狗。他喜欢在花园里玩柔软的蓝球。每天下午，麦克斯都在绿草地上奔跑。累了的时候，他就睡在温暖的篮子里。

questions.q: What color is Max the dog?
What toy does Max play with in the garden?
Where does Max sleep when he gets tired?

text.en: Lily went to the kitchen with her mother. She saw a big red apple on the table. Lily washed the apple with clean water. The apple tasted sweet and juicy.
text.zh: 莉莉和妈妈一起去了厨房。她看到桌子上有一个红红的大苹果。莉莉用干净的水洗了苹果。苹果尝起来又甜又多汁。

questions.q: Where did Lily go with her mother?
What fruit did Lily see on the table?
How did the apple taste?

text.en: Tom has a bright yellow kite. On windy days, he takes his kite to the park. The kite flies high up into the blue sky. Tom holds the string tightly and smiles.
text.zh: 汤姆有一个明黄色的风筝。在有风的日子里，他带着风筝去公园。风筝飞得高高的，飞进了蓝天。汤姆紧紧抓住线，笑了。

questions.q: What color is Tom's kite?
Where does Tom take his kite?
What does Tom hold tightly?

text.en: A tiny black ant walked near a tall flower. It found a small piece of sweet bread on the ground. The ant carried the bread back to its underground home to share with its friends.
text.zh: 一只黑色的小蚂蚁在一朵高高的花旁边爬行。它在地上发现了一小块甜面包。蚂蚁把面包搬回地下的家，和朋友们一起分享。

questions.q: What color was the ant?
What did the ant find on the ground?
Where did the ant take the food?

text.en: Rain began to fall outside the window. Emma put on her yellow raincoat and bright red boots. She stepped into a small puddle and giggled as the water splashed around.
text.zh: 窗外下起了雨。艾玛穿上黄色雨衣和红色的亮皮靴。她踏进一个小水坑里，当水花四溅时咯咯笑了起来。

questions.q: What color was Emma's raincoat?
What kind of shoes did Emma wear?
What did Emma step into?

text.en: A little blue bird sat on a high tree branch. Its mother brought a fat green worm. The baby bird ate the worm happily and flapped its wings to learn how to fly.
text.zh: 一只蓝色的小鸟站在高高的树枝上。鸟妈妈带来了一条肥肥的绿虫子。小鸟高兴地吃了虫子，拍打着翅膀学飞。

questions.q: Where was the little blue bird sitting?
What food did the mother bird bring?
Why did the baby bird flap its wings?

text.en: Sam got a shiny red toy car for his birthday. The car has four fast wheels and two bright lights. Sam loves pushing the car across the living room carpet.
text.zh: 萨姆过生日时得到了一辆闪亮的红玩具车。这辆车有四个快速轮子和两盏亮灯。萨姆喜欢把车推过客厅的地毯。

questions.q: Why did Sam get a toy car?
What color is the toy car?
Where does Sam push the car?

text.en: Ben sits at the table every morning. His grandmother pours him a glass of cold white milk. Ben drinks it all and eats a warm slice of toasted bread.
text.zh: 本每天早上都坐在桌前。奶奶给他倒了一杯冰凉的白牛奶。本一口气喝完，吃了一片温暖的烤面包。

questions.q: Who pours milk for Ben?
What does Ben drink every morning?
What does Ben eat with his milk?
options: A warm slice of toasted bread

text.en: Snowy is a cute white bunny with long pink ears. She likes eating fresh orange carrots. When Snowy is happy, she wiggles her twitchy nose and hops high.
text.zh: 斯诺伊是一只可爱的白兔，长着长长的粉红耳朵。她喜欢吃新鲜的橙色胡萝卜。斯诺伊开心的时候，就会耸耸小鼻子，跳得高高的。

questions.q: What kind of pet is Snowy?
What color are Snowy's ears?
What vegetable does Snowy like eating?

text.en: Mia opened a purple shoebox. Inside were new white sneakers with sparkly silver stars. Mia put them on and ran around the yard to test how fast she could go.
text.zh: 米亚打开了一个紫色的鞋盒。里面是一双带有闪亮银色星星的新白运动鞋。米亚穿上它们，在院子里跑来跑去，测试自己能跑多快。

questions.q: What color was the shoebox?
What was printed on the white sneakers?
Why did Mia run around the yard?
options: To test her fast new shoes

text.en: Tim has a small green turtle named Toby. Toby lives in a shallow glass tank with smooth river stones. Toby walks slowly under a leaf when he wants to rest.
text.zh: 蒂姆有一只名叫做托比的绿色小乌龟。托比住在带光滑河石的水槽里。当托比想休息时，他就慢慢爬到树叶下。

questions.q: What is the turtle's name?
What is inside Toby's glass tank?
What does Toby do when he wants to rest?

text.en: At sunset, a green frog sat on a broad lily pad in the quiet pond. The frog closed its eyes and made a loud ribbit sound to sing a song for the starry night.
text.zh: 傍晚时分，一只绿色的青蛙坐在安静池塘的阔荷叶上。青蛙闭上眼睛，发出响亮的呱呱声，为繁星点点的夜晚唱歌。

questions.q: Where did the green frog sit?
When did the frog sing?
What sound did the frog make?

text.en: Anna and her dad baked blueberry muffins in the kitchen. Anna stirred the sweet batter in a big yellow bowl. When the muffins came out of the oven, the house smelled delicious.
text.zh: 安娜和爸爸在厨房里烤蓝莓玛芬蛋糕。安娜在大黄碗里搅拌甜面糊。当玛芬从烤箱里出来时，屋子里弥漫着诱人的香味。

questions.q: What kind of muffins did Anna bake?
What color was the mixing bowl?
How did the house smell when the muffins were done?

text.en: Every morning, a bright red bus drives down Main Street. Children smile and wave from the glass windows. The friendly driver honks the horn twice as the bus stops near school.
text.zh: 每天早上，一辆鲜红色的公交车在主街上行驶。孩子们透过玻璃窗微笑挥手。当公交车停在学校附近时，友好的司机按了两次喇叭。

questions.q: What color is the bus?
Where do the children wave from?
How many times does the driver honk the horn?

text.en: Leo went to the neighborhood library on Saturday. He picked out a picture book about colorful sea fish. Leo sat on a soft blue cushion and read quietly.
text.zh: 里奥周六去了附近的图书馆。他挑了一本关于彩色海水鱼的绘本。里奥坐在软软的蓝垫子上静静地阅读。

questions.q: When did Leo go to the library?
What was the picture book about?
Where did Leo sit while reading?

text.en: Grandpa has a neat vegetable garden behind his house. He grows sweet tomatoes and crunchy cucumbers. Every morning, he uses a green watering can to feed his plants.
text.zh: 爷爷房后有一个整洁的菜园。他种了甜甜的番茄和脆脆的黄瓜。每天早上，他都用绿色浇水壶给植物浇水。

questions.q: Where is Grandpa's vegetable garden?
What vegetables does Grandpa grow?
What tool does Grandpa use to water his plants?

text.en: Ella looked for her fuzzy brown teddy bear, Barnaby. She checked under the bed and behind the door. Finally, she found Barnaby sitting safely on her wooden desk.
text.zh: 艾拉寻找她那只毛茸茸的棕色泰迪熊巴纳比。她检查了床底和门后。终于，她发现巴纳比安安静静地坐在她的木桌上。

questions.q: What is the name of Ella's teddy bear?
What color is the teddy bear?
Where did Ella find her teddy bear?

text.en: On a warm morning, Jack squeezed three sweet ripe oranges into a pitcher. He poured the bright orange juice into a glass and added two ice cubes to keep it cold.
text.zh: 在炎热的早晨，杰克把三个甜美的熟橙子挤进水壶里。他把鲜橙汁倒进玻璃杯里，加了两个冰块保温降温。

questions.q: How many oranges did Jack squeeze?
Where did Jack pour the fresh juice?
Why did Jack add ice cubes?

text.en: Whiskers is a white fluffy cat who loves sunbeams. She stretches on the warm wooden floor near the window. When you stroke her back, she purrs softly.
text.zh: 威斯克斯是一只喜欢阳光的蓬松白猫。她在窗边温暖的木地板上伸展身体。当你抚摸她的背部时，她会发出温柔的呼噜声。

questions.q: What color is Whiskers the cat?
Where does Whiskers stretch?
What sound does Whiskers make when stroked?

text.en: Noah walked along a quiet dirt path with his father. They saw tiny pine cones and red leaves on the ground. A brown squirrel scampered quickly up a tall pine tree.
text.zh: 诺亚和爸爸沿着一条安静的土路散步。他们看见地上有小松果和红叶子。一只棕色的松鼠快速爬上一棵高大的松树。

questions.q: Who walked with Noah in the woods?
What did Noah see on the ground?
What animal ran up a pine tree?

text.en: After the morning rain stopped, a giant colorful arc appeared over the green hill. Maya pointed at the rainbow and counted seven beautiful colors in the bright sky.
text.zh: 晨雨停后，绿色的山丘上出现了一条巨大的彩色弧线。玛雅指着彩虹，数着晴空中七种美丽的颜色。

questions.q: When did the rainbow appear?
Where did the rainbow appear?
How many colors did Maya count?

text.en: Lucas and his sister visited a calm blue lake. They threw small bits of dry bread into the water. Three mother ducks and five fluffy yellow ducklings swam over quickly.
text.zh: 卢卡斯和姐姐参观了一个平静的蓝色湖泊。他们把小块干面包扔进水里。三只母鸭和五只黄绒绒的小鸭子迅速游了过来。

questions.q: Where did Lucas and his sister go?
What food did they throw into the water?
How many yellow ducklings swam over?

text.en: Chloe spent the sunny morning at a fruit farm. She picked sweet red strawberries from green vines. She filled her small wicker basket to the top with fresh berries.
text.zh: 克洛伊在一个阳光明媚的早晨度过了水果农场之旅。她从绿色的藤蔓上摘下了甜甜的红草莓。她用新鲜的浆果装满了她的小柳条篮。

questions.q: Where did Chloe spend her morning?
What fruit did Chloe pick?
What did Chloe fill with berries?

text.en: Heavy snow fell all night. In the morning, David rolled three white snowballs in the yard. He gave his snowman a pointy orange carrot nose and a red wool scarf.
text.zh: 整晚都在下大雪。早上，大卫在院子里滚了三个白雪球。他给他的雪人装了一个尖尖的橙色胡萝卜鼻子和一条红羊毛围巾。

questions.q: How many snowballs did David roll?
What did David use for the snowman's nose?
What color scarf did David put on the snowman?

text.en: Oliver built a tiny boat from light pine wood. He placed it carefully into a trickling stream in the park. The little boat floated smoothly downstream past smooth gray pebbles.
text.zh: 奥利弗用松木做了一艘微型小船。他小心翼翼地把它放进公园细流淌的小溪里。小船顺流而下，滑过平滑的灰色小卵石。

questions.q: What material did Oliver use to build his boat?
Where did Oliver place his tiny boat?
What did the boat float past?

text.en: On Sunday morning, Grace visited her uncle's countryside farm. She helped feed the brown chickens with yellow corn seeds. Later, she brushed the soft coat of a little white pony named Star. Grace drank a glass of fresh milk before heading home in the afternoon.
text.zh: 周日早上，格蕾丝参观了叔叔的乡村农场。她帮忙用黄玉米粒喂棕色的母鸡。后来，她刷了一匹名叫斯塔的小白马柔软的毛发。下午回家前，格蕾丝喝了一杯新鲜牛奶。

questions.q: Whose farm did Grace visit?
What food did Grace give to the chickens?
What was the name of the white pony?
What did Grace drink before going home?

text.en: Nippy the squirrel lived inside a hollow oak tree. Every autumn, Nippy collected crunchy brown acorns and hid them in secret spots under fallen leaves. When winter came, he dug up his stored nuts to eat cozy inside his warm nest.
text.zh: 小松鼠尼皮住在空心的橡树里。每年秋天，尼皮都会收集脆脆的棕色橡实，隐藏在落叶下的秘密地点。当冬天来临时，他挖出储存的坚果，在温暖的巢穴里舒服地享用。

questions.q: Where did Nippy the squirrel live?
What food did Nippy collect in autumn?
Where did Nippy hide his acorns?
When did Nippy dig up his stored food?

text.en: Jake and his big brother pitched a blue tent in their quiet backyard. As the yellow moon rose, they roasted marshmallows over a small campfire. They listened to crickets chirping softly in the grass before falling asleep in cozy sleeping bags.
text.zh: 杰克和哥哥在安静的后院搭了一个蓝色的帐篷。当黄月亮升起时，他们在小营火上烤棉花糖。他们听着草丛里蟋蟀柔和的鸣叫声，然后在舒适的睡袋里入睡。

questions.q: Where did Jake and his brother pitch their tent?
What color was the tent?
What snack did they roast over the campfire?
What sound did they hear in the grass?

text.en: Sophie spent a hot afternoon at the ocean beach. She filled a plastic bucket with damp sand and made four tall towers for her sandcastle. She poked a tiny red paper flag into the top tower and decorated the walls with shiny white seashells.
text.zh: 索菲在海滩上度过了炎热的下午。她用湿沙填满了一个塑料桶，为她的沙堡造了四座高塔。她在顶塔上插了一面小红纸旗，并用闪亮的白贝壳装饰墙壁。

questions.q: Where did Sophie spend her afternoon?
How many towers did Sophie make?
What did Sophie put on the top tower?
What did Sophie use to decorate the sandcastle walls?

text.en: Beep is a friendly silver toy robot with glowing blue eyes. When Alex presses a red button on Beep's chest, the robot zooms forward and picks up scattered crayons from the floor. Beep places every crayon neatly inside a wooden box.
text.zh: 比普是一个友好的银色玩具机器人，长着闪烁的蓝眼睛。当亚历克斯按下比普胸前红按钮时，机器人向前冲去，拾起地板上散落的蜡笔。比普把每支蜡笔整齐地放进木盒子里。

questions.q: What color is the toy robot Beep?
Where is the red button located?
What items does Beep pick up from the floor?
Where does Beep place the crayons?

text.en: Maya's class went on a field trip to the city zoo. First, they saw two giant pandas chewing green bamboo leaves. Next, they watched playful river otters sliding down slippery rocks into the water. Maya bought a small panda magnet at the souvenir shop.
text.zh: 玛雅的班级去城市动物园郊游。首先，他们看到两只大熊猫在咀嚼绿竹叶。接下来，他们看着活泼的水獭沿着滑溜溜的石头滑进水里。玛雅在纪念品店买了一个小熊猫磁铁。

questions.q: Where did Maya's class go for their trip?
What were the giant pandas eating?
What animals slid down slippery rocks?
What souvenir did Maya buy?

text.en: Liam sat at his art desk with a fresh white paper. He dipped his wooden paintbrush into bright yellow paint to draw a glowing sun. He added green trees and a tiny blue cottage. Liam gave the finished painting to his grandmother.
text.zh: 里亚姆坐在他的艺术桌旁，拿出一张崭新的白纸。他把木制画笔浸入明黄色的颜料中，画出了耀眼的太阳。他添加了绿树和一座小蓝小屋。里亚姆把画好的作品送给了奶奶。

questions.q: What did Liam draw first with yellow paint?
What color was the small cottage in the painting?
What kind of paper did Liam use?
Who did Liam give his painting to?

text.en: During a boat trip in the calm ocean, Henry spotted a grey dolphin leaping out of the sparkling blue water. The dolphin swam alongside the boat and did two high flips in the air. Everyone on board clapped their hands excitedly.
text.zh: 在平静的海洋船游中，亨利看到一只灰色的海豚跃出闪烁的蓝水。海豚沿着船游，在空中翻了两个高难度的高空翻滚。船上的每个人都兴奋地鼓掌。

questions.q: What color was the dolphin Henry saw?
Where was Henry when he saw the dolphin?
options: During a boat trip in the ocean

questions.q: What trick did the dolphin do in the air?
How did the people on the boat react?

text.en: On a hot summer afternoon, Zoe squeezed six sour yellow lemons into a big glass jar. She added four spoons of white sugar and cold spring water. She stirred it with a wooden spoon and poured glasses for her thirsty friends.
text.zh: 在一个炎热的夏日下午，佐伊把六个酸酸的黄柠檬挤进一个大玻璃罐里。她加了四匙白糖和凉爽的泉水。她用木勺搅拌，给口渴的朋友倒了柠檬水。

questions.q: How many lemons did Zoe squeeze?
What sweetener did Zoe add to the pitcher?
What kind of spoon did Zoe use to stir?
Who did Zoe pour the lemonade for?

text.en: Oliver planted a small dark seed in a pot of dark soil. He watered it carefully every morning and placed it near the sunny window. After two weeks, a green shoot pushed through the dirt and grew a tiny yellow flower.
text.zh: 奥利弗在土盆里种下了一粒小小的黑种子。他每天早上仔细地浇水，并把它放在阳光明媚的窗户旁。两周后，一株绿芽破土而出，开出了一朵微黄的花朵。

questions.q: Where did Oliver plant the small dark seed?
options: In a pot of dark soil

questions.q: Where did Oliver place the pot?
How long did it take for the green shoot to push through?
What grew on the green shoot?

text.en: Lucas and his mom secretly baked a round vanilla cake for his sister's birthday. They spread sweet pink strawberry frosting over the top and placed seven glowing candles. When his sister walked into the room, everyone shouted Happy Birthday!
text.zh: 卢卡斯和妈妈秘密地为妹妹的生日烤了一个香草圆蛋糕。他们在顶部抹上甜甜的粉色草莓糖霜，安放了七支点燃的蜡烛。当妹妹走进房间时，大家都大喊生日快乐！

questions.q: What flavor was the surprise birthday cake?
What kind of frosting did they spread on the cake?
How many candles were placed on top?
What did everyone shout when the sister entered?

text.en: Ethan practiced riding his new red bicycle on the paved park trail. His father held the back of the seat to help him balance. After three tries, Ethan pedaled all by himself while wearing his blue safety helmet.
text.zh: 伊桑在公园铺好的小径上练习骑他的新红自行车。爸爸握着车座后部帮他保持平衡。尝试了三次后，伊桑戴着蓝色安全头盔自己踩动脚踏板前进。

questions.q: Where did Ethan practice riding his bicycle?
Who helped Ethan balance his bike?
How many tries did it take for Ethan to ride alone?
What safety gear did Ethan wear on his head?

text.en: During October, the leaves on the big maple tree turned bright red and orange. Hannah and her little brother raked the fallen leaves into a giant soft pile. They took a deep breath and jumped right into the middle of the crisp leaves.
text.zh: 在十月份，大枫树上的树叶变成了鲜艳的红色和橙色。汉娜和弟弟把落叶扫成一个巨大的软堆。他们深深吸了一口气，然后径直跳进了脆脆的树叶堆里。

questions.q: What month did the maple leaves change color?
What colors did the maple leaves turn?
What did Hannah and her brother do with the leaves?
options: Raked them into a giant soft pile

questions.q: What fun action did they do into the leaf pile?

text.en: Mason visited a large city aquarium with his family. They walked through an underwater glass tunnel while giant manta rays and colorful tropical fish swam overhead. Mason enjoyed watching a sea otter float on its back while eating a clam.
text.zh: 梅森和家人一起参观了一个大型城市水族馆。他们走过水下玻璃隧道，头顶游过巨大的蝠鲼和彩色的热带鱼。梅森喜欢看海獭仰泳吃蛤蜊。

questions.q: What special feature did Mason walk through at the aquarium?
What sea creatures swam overhead in the tunnel?
options: Giant manta rays and tropical fish

questions.q: What animal did Mason enjoy watching?
What was the sea otter doing while floating?

text.en: Mrs. Potts owns a tiny bakery on Maple Street. Every morning at five o'clock, she bakes warm golden loaves of bread and sweet cinnamon rolls. Neighbors line up outside the door because the delicious smell fills the whole street.
text.zh: 波茨夫人在枫树街开了一家微型面包店。每天早晨五点钟，她都烤制出金黄温暖的面包和甜甜的肉桂卷。邻居们在门外排起长队，因为诱人的香味弥漫了整条街。

questions.q: What is the name of the bakery owner?
What time does Mrs. Potts start baking?
options: At five o'clock in the morning

questions.q: What baked goods does Mrs. Potts make?
options: Golden loaves of bread and cinnamon rolls

questions.q: Why do neighbors line up outside the bakery?
options: Because the delicious smell fills the street

text.en: On a crisp Saturday afternoon, Alex and his grandfather decided to build a wooden birdhouse for the garden. First, Grandfather carefully measured and sawed four flat pine boards into neat pieces. Next, Alex used a small metal hammer to tap short shiny nails into the wood to form walls and a roof. They painted the outside of the birdhouse with bright blue weather-proof paint. Finally, they tied the new birdhouse securely to a sturdy branch of a tall oak tree. By Sunday evening, a pair of chirping bluebirds had already moved in.
text.zh: 在一个爽朗的周六下午，亚历克斯和爷爷决定为花园制作一个木鸟窝。首先，爷爷仔细测量并锯开四块平整的松木板成整齐的块。接下来，亚历克斯用一把小铁锤把短亮的钉子打入木头里，形成墙壁和屋顶。他们用鲜艳的蓝色防水漆涂抹了鸟窝的外观。最后，他们把新鸟窝紧紧系在一棵高大橡树的结实树枝上。到了周日晚上，一对唧唧喳喳的蓝鸟已经搬了进来。

questions.q: Who helped Alex build the wooden birdhouse?
What tool did Alex use to drive the nails into the wood?
What color paint did they use for the birdhouse?
Where did they tie the finished birdhouse?
options: To a branch of a tall oak tree
On the roof of the porch

questions.q: What kind of birds moved into the birdhouse by Sunday evening?

text.en: Honeybees are remarkable little insects that work together in a busy colony inside a wooden hive. The queen bee lays all the tiny eggs, while thousands of female worker bees do many important jobs. Worker bees fly from flower to flower gathering sweet nectar and golden pollen. They use their long straw-like tongues to sip nectar and carry it back to the hive in special honey sacs. Inside the hive, they fan their wings rapidly to evaporate water from the nectar, transforming it into thick sweet honey. Honeybees also help flowers grow by spreading pollen between plants.
text.zh: 蜜蜂是了不起的小昆虫，在一个木制蜂箱里的忙碌群体中协同工作。蜂后产下所有微小的蛋，而数以千计的女工蜂承担着许多重要的工作。工蜂在花丛间飞来飞去，收集甜美的花蜜和金黄的花粉。它们用像吸管一样长长的舌头吸吮花蜜，用特殊的蜜囊把花蜜带回蜂巢。在蜂巢内部，它们快速扇动翅膀蒸发花蜜中的水分，将其转化为浓稠甜美的蜂蜜。蜜蜂还通过在植物间传播花粉来帮助鲜花生长。

questions.q: What job does the queen bee have in the colony?
What do female worker bees gather from flowers?
What body part do bees use to sip nectar?
How do worker bees evaporate water from nectar inside the hive?
options: By storing it in the sun

questions.q: How do honeybees help plants and flowers grow?

title.en: A Day at the Science Museum

text.en: Class 2B took an exciting field trip to the National Science Museum. In the first hall, students explored giant interactive models of space rockets and satellite craft. Next, they visited the physics station where they learned how magnets pull heavy iron objects using invisible magnetic force fields. The highlight of the trip was a live demonstration where a scientist generated indoor lightning bolts using a powerful Tesla coil generator. Every student received a small magnifying glass as a gift before boarding the school bus.
text.zh: 二B班去国家科技馆进行了一次令人兴奋的郊游。在第一个大厅里，同学们探索了宇宙火箭和卫星飞行器的巨型互动模型。接下来，他们参观了物理站，在那里他们了解了磁铁如何利用无形的磁场力吸引沉重的铁物体。这次旅行的亮点是一场现场演示，一名科学家使用强大的特斯拉线圈发电机在室内生成闪电。在登上校车之前，每个学生都获得了一面小放大镜作为礼物。

questions.q: Which museum hall did Class 2B explore first?
What force pulls iron objects at the physics station?
What was the highlight demonstration at the museum?
options: Creating indoor lightning with a Tesla coil

questions.q: Who generated the indoor lightning bolts?
What gift did every student receive before leaving?

text.en: Sea turtles are ancient ocean reptiles that swim thousands of miles across open seas. Female sea turtles return to the exact sandy beach where they were born to lay their eggs. Under the moonlight, a mother turtle digs a deep hole in the warm sand with her hind flippers. She lays around one hundred soft white eggs and covers them gently before crawling back into the waves. Two months later, tiny hatchlings break out of their shells and race across the sand toward the ocean foam.
text.zh: 海龟是古老的海洋爬行动物，在大海上游泳数千英里。雌海龟回到它们出生时的确切沙滩产卵。在月光下，母海龟用后鳍肢在温暖的沙滩上挖了一个深坑。她产下大约一百个软软的白蛋，轻轻盖上，然后爬回浪花中。两个月后，微小的幼龟破壳而出，穿过沙滩奔向海洋泡泡。

questions.q: Where do female sea turtles lay their eggs?
options: On the beach where they were born

questions.q: What body part does the mother turtle use to dig the nest?
About how many eggs does a mother sea turtle lay?
How long does it take for hatchlings to break out of their shells?
Where do tiny hatchlings race after hatching?

text.en: Guided by an experienced instructor, Maya and her family explored a cool limestone cave deep under a hill. They wore bright yellow helmets equipped with strong forehead headlamps. Inside, cool water dripped from sharp rocky icicles called stalactites hanging from the high ceiling. On the ground, matching mineral cones called stalagmites grew slowly upward from the damp floor over hundreds of years. The guide pointed out a small cluster of sleeping brown bats resting high above.
text.zh: 在经验丰富的导师指导下，玛雅和家人探索了山深处凉爽的灰岩洞。他们戴着装有强力额头头灯的鲜黄色头盔。在洞内，冰凉的水滴从挂在高天花板上被称为钟乳石的尖石冰柱上滴下。在地面上，被称为石笋的匹配矿物锥在数百年的时间里从湿漉漉的地板慢慢向上生长。导游指着挂在高处的一小群冬眠中的棕色蝙蝠。

questions.q: What kind of cave did Maya and her family explore?
What equipment did they wear on their heads?
What are the sharp mineral formations hanging from the ceiling called?
Where do stalagmites grow from?
What animals did the guide point out sleeping high above?
options: A cluster of sleeping brown bats

text.en: Sunflowers are famous for their unique habit called heliotropism, which means following the sun. In the early morning, young sunflower buds face east toward the rising sun. As the sun moves across the sky during the day, the flower head slowly turns westward to follow the light. At night, the plant turns back east to prepare for the morning dawn. When the sunflower reaches full maturity, its thick stalk hardens in place facing east. Eventually, the heavy yellow flower head produces hundreds of nutritious black seeds.
text.zh: 向日葵因其被称为向日性的独特习惯而闻名，意为跟随太阳。在清晨，年轻的向日葵花蕾朝东面向升起的太阳。白天太阳在空中移动时，花头慢慢向西转动以跟随光明。夜间，植物转回东方以迎晨曦。当向日葵达到完全成熟时，其粗壮的茎硬化停在朝东的位置。最终，沉甸甸的黄花头结出数百粒营养丰富的黑种子。

questions.q: What does the word heliotropism mean for sunflowers?
Which direction do young sunflower buds face in the early morning?
What happens to the flower head as the sun moves during the day?
options: It turns westward to follow the light

questions.q: Which way does a mature sunflower stalk harden and face?
What does a fully grown sunflower head produce?

text.en: Long ago in ancient China, a clever court official named Cai Lun invented a practical way to make paper. Before his invention, people wrote important words on heavy bamboo strips or expensive silk cloth. Cai Lun mixed tree bark, old rags, and hemp fibers with water into a watery pulp. He pressed the wet pulp flat onto a woven bamboo screen and allowed it to dry thoroughly in the sun. This created thin, lightweight sheets of paper that were cheap to produce. Cai Lun's invention spread across the world and changed how humans share knowledge.
text.zh: 很久以前在中国古代，一位名叫蔡伦的聪慧官员发明了一种实用的造纸方法。在他发明之前，人们把重要的文字写在沉重的竹简或昂贵的丝绸布上。蔡伦将树皮、旧布和麻纤维与水混合成稀薄的纸浆。他把湿纸浆平压在编织的竹筛上，放在太阳下彻底晒干。这创造出了生产成本低廉的薄型轻便纸张。蔡伦的发明传遍全世界，改变了人类分享知识的方式。

questions.q: Who invented a practical way to make paper in ancient China?
What heavy material did people write on before paper was invented?
What ingredients did Cai Lun mix with water to create pulp?
options: Tree bark, old rags, and hemp

questions.q: How was the wet pulp dried into paper sheets?
Why was Cai Lun's paper a great improvement?
options: It was thin, lightweight, and cheap to produce
It could glow in the dark

text.en: Monarch butterflies are famous for their extraordinary annual journey across North America. Every autumn, millions of orange-and-black butterflies fly over two thousand miles south to reach warm mountain forests in Mexico. During the cold winter months, they cluster tightly together on fir tree trunks to stay warm and conserve energy. When spring arrives, the monarchs wake up, mate, and begin flying north again. Along the way, females lay green eggs exclusively on milkweed plants, which serve as the only food source for hatching caterpillars.
text.zh: 黑脉金斑蝶以其一年一度横跨北美洲的非凡旅程而闻名。每年秋天，数以百万计的黑橙相间的蝴蝶飞越两千多英里前往墨西哥温暖的山区森林。在寒冷的冬季，它们紧紧聚拢在杉树干上保温并节省精力。当春天来临时，黑脉金斑蝶醒来，交配，并开始再次向北飞行。在途中，雌蝶专门在乳草植物上产下绿蛋，乳草是孵化出的毛毛虫唯一的食物来源。

questions.q: What colors are monarch butterflies?
Where do millions of monarchs fly every autumn?
options: To warm mountain forests in Mexico

questions.q: How do monarchs stay warm on fir trees during winter?
When do monarchs begin their return trip north?
What is the only plant hatching monarch caterpillars eat?

text.en: A rainbow is a beautiful optical phenomenon created by sunlight interacting with water droplets in the atmosphere. When sunlight passes into a spherical raindrop, the liquid acts like a tiny glass prism. The white sunlight bends, or refracts, and splits into its component spectrum of seven distinct colors: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet. The light then reflects off the back wall of the raindrop and bounces out into the sky. You can only see a rainbow when the sun is shining behind you and rain is falling in front of you.
text.zh: 彩虹是一种美丽的光学现象，由阳光与大气中的水滴相互作用产生。当阳光穿过球形雨滴时，液体就像一个微小的玻璃棱镜。白色的阳光弯曲或折射，并分解为其由七种不同颜色组成的成分光谱：红、橙、黄、绿、蓝、靛、紫。然后光线从雨滴后壁反射并弹射到空中。只有当太阳在身后照射，雨水在面前落下时，你才能看到彩虹。

questions.q: What causes a rainbow to form in the sky?
How does a spherical raindrop act when sunlight enters it?
What scientific process bends sunlight inside the droplet?
How many colors make up the visible rainbow spectrum?
Where must the sun be located for a person to see a rainbow?

text.en: Beavers are famous natural engineers of the animal kingdom. They construct sturdy wooden dams across freshwater streams to create calm, deep ponds. Using their powerful jaw muscles and orange front teeth, beavers gnaw down wooden tree trunks and thick branches. They drag the logs into the flowing stream and interlock them with mud, stones, and river weeds to stop the water flow. In the middle of the quiet pond, the beaver family builds a dome-shaped wooden lodge with underwater entrances. This safe home keeps them warm and protects them from predators like wolves and bears.
text.zh: 河狸是动物界著名的天然工程大师。它们在淡水小溪上建造坚固的木制水坝，创造出平静的深水塘。河狸利用强大的颌肌和橙色的门齿咬断木质树干和粗树枝。它们把木头拖进流动的小溪里，用泥土、石头和河草将它们咬合在一起，以阻断水流。在平静的水塘中央，河狸一家建造了一个圆顶木小屋，带有水下入口。这个安全的地方保暖并保护它们免受狼和熊等捕食者的侵害。

questions.q: Why do beavers build wooden dams across streams?
What body feature allows beavers to gnaw down tree trunks?
options: Orange front teeth and jaw muscles

questions.q: What materials do beavers use to seal gaps between logs?
Where is the beaver lodge built?
options: In the middle of the quiet pond

questions.q: Why does the beaver lodge have underwater entrances?
options: To protect them from predators like wolves

text.en: Every year when autumn arrives, billions of birds embark on incredible long-distance migratory journeys across continents. As the days grow shorter and temperatures drop, food sources like insects and berries become scarce in northern regions. Birds travel thousands of miles to warmer southern climates where food is abundant. How do birds navigate across vast oceans and unfamiliar landscapes without getting lost? Scientists have discovered that migratory birds rely on a combination of incredible natural navigation tools. They use the position of the sun during the day and star patterns at night. In addition, birds possess a special internal magnetic sense that allows them to detect Earth's magnetic field like an invisible compass. Some species even remember visual landmarks, such as coastline shapes and major river valleys. Before starting their journey, birds eat heavily to store body fat, which serves as vital fuel for non-stop flights across vast distances.
text.zh: 每年当秋天到来时，数十亿只鸟类踏上不可思议的大洲间长途迁徙之旅。随着白天变短、气温下降，昆虫和浆果等食物来源在北方地区变得稀少。鸟类飞行数千英里前往食物丰富的南方温暖气候区。鸟类如何在没有迷路的情况下穿越浩瀚的海洋和不熟悉的景象？科学家们发现，迁徙鸟类依赖一系列不可思议的天然导航工具组合。它们白天利用太阳的位置，夜晚利用星星的排列。此外，鸟类拥有一项特殊的内部磁觉，使它们能够像隐形指南针一样探测地球的磁场。有些物种甚至能记住视觉地标，比如海岸线形状和大河谷。在开旅程之前，鸟类大量进食以储存脂肪，这是跨越漫长距离不间断飞行的重要燃料。

questions.q: Why do birds migrate south when autumn arrives?
options: Because northern food sources become scarce

questions.q: What celestial object do birds use for navigation during the day?
What do birds use at night to stay on course?
What special internal sense helps birds detect Earth's magnetic field?
What visual landmarks do some bird species remember during flight?
Why do birds eat heavily right before embarking on their journey?
options: To store body fat as vital flight fuel

text.en: Unlike animals that must eat food to survive, green plants have the amazing ability to generate their own nourishment through a process called photosynthesis. This complex chemical process takes place inside tiny microscopic structures in plant leaves called chloroplasts. Chloroplasts contain a green pigment called chlorophyll, which absorbs light energy from the sun. Leaves pull in carbon dioxide gas from the surrounding air through microscopic pores on their undersides called stomata. Meanwhile, plant roots draw up fresh water and essential minerals from the soil. Using the trapped solar energy, the plant combines carbon dioxide and water to produce a sweet glucose sugar, which feeds the plant and fuels its growth. As a beneficial byproduct of photosynthesis, the plant releases clean oxygen gas back into the atmosphere. Without green plants performing photosynthesis, humans and animals would not have oxygen to breathe or food to eat.
text.zh: 与必须进食食物才能生存的动物不同，绿色植物具有通过称为光合作用的过程产生自身营养的惊人能力。这一复杂的化学过程发生在植物叶片中被称为叶绿体的微观结构内部。叶绿体含有称为叶绿素的绿色色素，能吸收来自太阳的光能。叶片通过背面被称为气孔的微观小孔从周围空气中吸入二氧化碳气体。同时，植物根部从土壤中汲取新鲜水分和必需矿物质。利用捕获的太阳能，植物将二氧化碳和水结合产生甜葡萄糖，为植物提供养分并促进其生长。作为光合作用的有益副产品，植物将干净的氧气释放回大气中。如果没有绿色植物进行光合作用，人类和动物将没有氧气呼吸或食物进食。

questions.q: What is the process green plants use to generate their own food called?
Inside which microscopic leaf structures does photosynthesis take place?
What green pigment inside leaves absorbs solar energy?
What are the microscopic pores on the underside of leaves called?
What sweet substance does the plant create to feed itself?
What crucial byproduct does photosynthesis release into the air?

text.en: Coral reefs are often called the underwater rainforests of the ocean because they support an astonishing variety of marine life. Although coral structures look like colorful ocean rocks or sea plants, they are actually built by millions of tiny soft animals called coral polyps. These polyps construct hard calcium carbonate skeletons around themselves for protection. Over hundreds of years, billions of these stony skeletons accumulate to create massive underwater reef ecosystems. Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, yet they provide shelter, food, and breeding grounds for over twenty-five percent of all ocean species. Bright clownfish hide safely among stinging sea anemone tentacles, while sea turtles and reef sharks patrol the warm blue waters. Unfortunately, coral reefs are delicate and face serious threats from ocean pollution, rising water temperatures, and destructive fishing practices. Protecting these marine habitats is vital for maintaining ocean biodiversity.
text.zh: 珊瑚礁常被称为海洋的淡水雨林，因为它们支持着惊人多样的海洋生物。虽然珊瑚结构看起来像彩色的海洋岩石或海生植物，但它们实际上是由数以百万计的称为珊瑚虫的微小软体动物建造的。这些珊瑚虫在自身周围建造坚硬的碳酸钙骨骼以自我保护。数百年来，数以十亿计的这些石质骨骼堆积形成巨大的水下珊瑚礁生态系统。珊瑚礁占海底面积不到百分之一，但它们为超过四分之一的海洋物种提供庇护所、食物和繁殖场所。鲜艳的小丑鱼安全地隐藏在刺痛的海葵触手间，而海龟和礁鲨在温暖的蓝色水域巡逻。不幸的是，珊瑚礁非常脆弱，面临着海洋污染、水温上升和破坏性捕捞做法的严重威胁。保护这些海洋栖息地对于维持海洋生物多样性至关重要。

questions.q: Why are coral reefs referred to as the underwater rainforests of the ocean?
options: They support an astonishing variety of marine life

questions.q: What living organisms actually construct coral reef structures?
options: Tiny soft animals called coral polyps

questions.q: What mineral compound forms the hard skeletons of coral polyps?
About what percentage of all ocean species rely on coral reefs?
Where do bright clownfish hide for safety in the reef?
What serious threats do coral reefs face today?
options: Ocean pollution and rising water temperatures

text.en: Sound is an energy form created whenever an object vibrates rapidly back and forth. When a drumhead is struck, it vibrates and pushes against surrounding air molecules, creating invisible compression waves. These sound waves travel outward through the air in all directions, similar to ripples spreading across a quiet pond when a pebble is dropped. Sound requires a physical medium, such as air, water, or solid wood, to transmit its energy. Because space is a vacuum with no air molecules, sound cannot travel through outer space at all. Sound waves travel at different speeds depending on the density of the medium. For instance, sound travels through air at about 767 miles per hour, but it travels four times faster through liquid water and fifteen times faster through solid steel! When sound waves enter your outer ear, they cause your tiny eardrum to vibrate, allowing your brain to process sounds as music, speech, or noise.
text.zh: 每当物体快速前后振动时，就会创造出声音这种能量形式。当鼓面受到撞击时，它会振动并推压周围的空气分子，产生无形的压缩波。这些声波通过空气向各个方向向外传播，类似于石子落入平静水池时扩散的涟漪。声音需要物理介质（例如空气、水或实木）来传输其能量。因为太空是没有任何空气分子的真空，声音根本无法在外层空间传播。声波根据介质的密度以不同的速度传播。例如，声音在空气中以每小时约767英里的速度传播，但在液体水中传播速度快四倍，在固体钢中传播速度快十五倍！当声波进入你的外耳时，它们会导致你微小的鼓膜振动，让你的大脑将声音处理为音乐、言语或噪音。

questions.q: How is sound energy created?
options: Whenever an object vibrates rapidly back and forth

questions.q: What type of waves are produced when a drumhead vibrates?
Why can sound NOT travel through outer space?
options: Space is a vacuum with no air molecules

questions.q: How much faster does sound travel through water compared to air?
Through which material does sound travel fifteen times faster than through air?
What part of the human ear vibrates when sound waves enter it?

text.en: Our solar system is a vast cosmic family bound together by the powerful gravitational pull of the Sun. At the center sits the Sun, a massive glowing ball of hot hydrogen and helium plasma that contains over ninety-nine percent of all matter in the solar system. Orbiting around the Sun are eight major planets, which are divided into two distinct groups. The four inner planets—Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars—are small terrestrial worlds composed mainly of rock and metal. In contrast, the four outer planets—Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune—are giant gas and ice worlds with thick atmospheric layers and extensive ring systems. Beyond Neptune lies the Kuiper Belt, a icy region home to dwarf planets like Pluto and icy comets. Scientists use robotic space probes and giant space telescopes like Hubble and James Webb to capture incredible images and study these distant celestial frontiers.
text.zh: 我们的太阳系是一个巨大的宇宙家族，由太阳强大的万有引力紧紧联系在一起。太阳位于中心，是一个巨大的发光氢气和氦气等离子球，包含了太阳系中超过百分之九十九的所有物质。围绕太阳运行的是八大行星，分为两个不同的组。四大类地内行星——水星、金星、地球和火星——是由岩石和金属组成的小型陆地世界。相比之下，四大外行星——木星、土星、天王星和海王星——是拥有厚厚大气层和广泛环系的大型气体和冰雪世界。海王星之外是柯伊伯带，是一个冰冷的大区，是像冥王星这样的矮行星和冰彗星的家园。科学家们利用机器人太空探测器和哈勃、詹姆斯·韦伯等巨型太空望远镜拍摄令人难以置信的照片，并研究这些遥远的天体前沿。

questions.q: What gravitational force holds our solar system together?
options: The powerful gravitational pull of the Sun

questions.q: Which two hot gases make up the Sun?
Which four planets make up the small terrestrial inner planets?
What materials primarily compose the four outer gas giant planets?
options: Giant gas and ice with ring systems

questions.q: What icy region lies beyond Neptune where Pluto is located?
What instruments do astronomers use to capture images of distant planets?
options: Robotic space probes and space telescopes

text.en: Water on Earth is constantly moving and recycling through a continuous natural process known as the water cycle. The sun provides thermal energy that heats up liquid water in oceans, lakes, and rivers. As water warms, it transforms into an invisible gas called water vapor through evaporation. Plants also release water vapor into the air through their leaf pores in a process called transpiration. As the warm water vapor rises high into the atmosphere, it cools down and turns back into tiny liquid water droplets, forming clouds during condensation. When cloud droplets grow too heavy to stay suspended in the air, they fall back to Earth as precipitation in the form of rain, snow, sleet, or hail. This fallen water collects in rivers and streams, flowing back into the ocean to restart the endless cycle.
text.zh: 地球上的水不断在被称为水循环的连续自然过程中流动和循环利用。太阳提供热能，加热海洋、湖泊和河流中的液体水。随着水变热，它通过蒸发转化为一种被称为水蒸气的无形气体。植物还通过叶片孔在被称为蒸腾作用的过程中向空气中释放水蒸气。随着温热的水蒸气升入大气高处，它冷却并变回微小的液体水滴，在凝结过程中形成云。当云滴增长得太重而无法悬浮在空气中时，它们以雨、雪、雨夹雪或冰雹的形式作为降水落回地球。这些落下的水聚集在河流和小溪中，流回海洋，重新开始这永无止境的循环。

text.en: Today, bicycles are one of the most popular eco-friendly modes of transportation worldwide, but early designs were very different from modern bikes. In 1817, a German inventor named Baron Karl von Drais created the first wooden two-wheeled riding machine called the Running Machine. It had no pedals or chains; riders propelled themselves forward by pushing their feet against the ground while steering the front wheel. In the 1870s, inventors created the High-Wheel bicycle, also known as the Penny-Farthing, which featured a gigantic front wheel and a small rear wheel. Although it allowed riders to travel faster, it was dangerous because riders sat very high up and easily flipped forward over the handlebars. Finally, in 1885, John Kemp Starley invented the Safety Bicycle, which featured equal-sized wheels, a metal chain drive connected to rear pedals, and air-filled rubber tires. This revolutionary design made cycling safe, comfortable, and accessible for everyone.
text.zh: 如今，自行车是全球最受欢迎的环保交通工具之一，但早期设计与现代自行车大不相同。1817年，一位名叫卡尔·冯·德赖斯男爵的德国发明家创造了第一台木制双轮骑行机器，称为跑步机。它没有脚踏板或链条；骑行者通过脚抵地面推向前进，同时操纵前轮。在19世纪70年代，发明家们创造了高轮自行车，也称为便士法新自行车，其特征是一个巨大的前轮和一个小的后轮。虽然它允许骑行者行驶得更快，但它很危险，因为骑行者坐得非常高，很容易翻过车把摔倒。最后，在1885年，约翰·凯姆普·斯塔利发明了安全自行车，具有等大的车轮、连接到后踏板的金属链条驱动以及充气橡胶轮胎。这一革命性的设计使骑自行车对每个人来说都是安全、舒适和易于操作的。

text.en: Emperor penguins are the tallest and heaviest of all penguin species, uniquely adapted to survive the brutal freezing conditions of Antarctica. During the harsh Antarctic winter, temperatures plunge below minus fifty degrees Celsius with howling blizzard winds. While other polar animals flee north, female emperor penguins lay a single heavy egg on the ice and immediately trek to the ocean to feed for two months. The male penguin carefully balances the precious egg on top of his webbed feet, covering it with a warm feathered skin fold called a brood pouch. To survive freezing winds, male penguins form huge tightly packed huddles containing thousands of birds. They continuously rotate from the cold outer edges of the group to the warm interior, sharing body heat equally. When the females return from the sea with bellies full of fish, the chicks hatch, and the parents take turns guarding and feeding their growing young.
text.zh: 帝企鹅是所有企鹅物种中最高和最重的，经过独特的适应可以在南极洲残酷的冰冻条件下生存。在严酷的南极冬季，气温降至零下五十摄氏度以下，伴随着呼啸的暴风雪。当其他极地动物向北逃避时，母帝企鹅在冰上产下一个沉甸甸的蛋，并立即徒步前往海洋进食两个月。公企鹅小心翼翼地把珍贵的蛋平衡在蹼足顶端，用称为育儿袋的温暖羽毛皮肤褶皱覆盖着它。为了在冰冻的风中生存，公企鹅形成了包含数千只鸟的大型紧密拥挤群。它们不断从冷外缘轮流移动到温暖的内部，平等分享体温。当母企鹅满肚带着鱼从大海归来时，小企鹅孵化出来，父母轮流看守和喂养它们不断生长的幼鸟。

text.en: The Great Wall of China is one of the most magnificent architectural wonders ever created by human civilization. Stretching over thirteen thousand miles across rugged mountains, vast deserts, and rolling grasslands, this colossal fortification was constructed over many centuries by several ancient Chinese dynasties. The earliest sections were built over two thousand years ago during the Qin Dynasty under Emperor Qin Shi Huang to protect the northern borders from nomadic invasions. Millions of soldiers, farmers, and stonemasons cut giant blocks of granite, baked durable bricks, and mixed mortar made from sticky rice to construct the high protective walls. Watchtowers were positioned at regular intervals along the wall, allowing guards to signal incoming danger across long distances using smoke signals during the day and fiery torches at night. Today, the Great Wall stands as a proud symbol of China's rich history and attracts millions of international travelers each year.
text.zh: 中国长城是人类文明创造的最壮丽的建筑奇观之一。这座巨大的防御工事跨越崎岖的山脉、辽阔的沙漠和起伏的草地，绵延一万三千多英里，由中国古代几个朝代历经数个世纪建造而成。最早的章节建于两千多年前的秦朝，在秦始皇的领导下，旨在保护北部边境免受游牧民族的入侵。数以百万计的士兵、农民和石匠切割巨型花岗岩块，烘烤耐用的砖块，并用糯米制成的浆糊混合砂浆建造高大的保护墙。烽火台沿墙定期布置，允许卫兵白天使用烟雾信号，夜晚使用火把在长距离内传达即将到来的危险。如今，长城作为中国悠久历史的骄傲象征屹立不倒，每年吸引数以百万计的国际游客。

text.en: The deep ocean floor is the least explored environment on Earth, shrouded in pitch-black darkness and extreme water pressure. Descending beyond six thousand meters into deep ocean trenches like the Mariana Trench reveals a world devoid of sunlight. In this harsh abyss, water temperatures linger near freezing, yet unique deep-sea creatures have adapted to thrive. Many deep-sea fish, such as the anglerfish, produce their own glowing light through a natural chemical reaction called bioluminescence. The anglerfish uses a glowing lure dangling above its mouth to attract unsuspecting prey in the dark. Nearby, hydrothermal vents on the ocean floor spew superheated, mineral-rich water from deep inside the Earth's crust. Specialized giant tube worms and ghost crabs live around these hot vents without sunlight, deriving energy from sulfur-eating bacteria. Deep-sea exploration using advanced robotic submersibles continues to uncover new species and remarkable scientific secrets.
text.zh: 深海海底是地球上被探索最少的环境，笼罩在漆黑的黑暗和极度的水压中。下降到超过六千米深如马里亚纳海沟的深海海沟中，展现出一个没有阳光的世界。在这个严酷的深渊里，水温在冰点附近徘徊，然而独特的深海生物已经适应生存。许多深海鱼类，如鮟鱇鱼，通过被称为生物发光的天然化学反应产生自己的发光亮光。鮟鱇鱼使用悬挂在嘴上方的发光诱饵在黑暗中吸引不知情的猎物。在附近，海底的热液喷口从地球地壳深处喷出超热的、富含矿物质的水。专门的巨型管虫和幽灵蟹在这些热喷口周围生活，没有阳光，从吃硫磺的细菌中获取能量。使用先进机器人潜水器进行的深海探索继续发现新物种和非凡的科学秘密。

writing.zh: 什么是可怕的动物？

writing.zh: 当你生气时你会做什么？

text.en: Giant pandas live in the bamboo forests of central China. They have thick black-and-white fur that keeps them warm in cold mountain air. Pandas spend up to twelve hours a day chewing fresh green bamboo leaves.
text.zh: 大熊猫生活在中国中部的竹林里。它们有着厚厚的黑白相间的毛发，在寒冷的山区空气中保持温暖。熊猫一天花长达十二个小时咀嚼新鲜的绿竹叶。

questions.q: Where do giant pandas live?
options: In the bamboo forests of central China

questions.q: What helps pandas stay warm in cold mountain air?
How many hours a day can pandas spend eating bamboo?

text.en: Every green plant needs three basic things to grow: sunlight, water, and rich soil. Roots absorb water from the ground, while green leaves capture energy from the sun to make nutritious food.
text.zh: 每株绿色植物都需要三种基本的东西才能生长：阳光、水和肥沃的土壤。根部从地下吸收水分，而绿叶则捕捉来自太阳的能量来制造营养食物。

questions.q: What three basic things do green plants need to grow?
What part of the plant absorbs water from the ground?
What do green leaves capture from the sun?

text.en: The octopus is one of the smartest creatures in the sea. It has eight flexible arms lined with sensitive suction cups. When an octopus feels danger, it squirts a cloud of dark ink and swims away.
text.zh: 章鱼是海洋中最聪明的生物之一。它有八条灵活的喷有敏感吸盘的触手。当章鱼感受到危险时，它会喷出一云暗墨水并游走。

questions.q: How many flexible arms does an octopus have?
What lines the arms of an octopus?
What does an octopus squirt when it feels danger?

text.en: Leo and his family pitched their green tent near a quiet blue lake. During the day, they rowed a wooden canoe and caught two silvery fish. At night, they sat by a warm campfire and told stories.
text.zh: 里奥和家人在平静的蓝湖附近搭起了他们的绿帐篷。白天，他们划着木划艇，捕到了两条银色的鱼。晚上，他们坐在温暖的营火旁讲故事。

questions.q: Where did Leo and his family pitch their tent?
What activity did they do during the day?
What did they do at night by the campfire?

text.en: In 1891, a gym teacher named James Naismith invented basketball in Massachusetts. He nailed two peach baskets onto indoor balcony railings. Players scored points by throwing a heavy ball into the baskets.
text.zh: 1891年，一位名叫詹姆斯·奈史密斯的体育老师在马萨诸塞州发明了篮球。他把两个桃子筐钉在室内阳台栏杆上。球员们通过把重球扔进筐里来得分。

questions.q: Who invented the game of basketball in 1891?
What target did Naismith nail onto the balcony railings?
How did players score points in the early game?
options: By throwing a heavy ball into the baskets

text.en: Hummingbirds are the smallest birds in the world. Their tiny wings beat up to eighty times per second, making a soft humming noise. They hover in mid-air to drink sweet nectar from colorful flowers.
text.zh: 蜂鸟是世界上最小的鸟类。它们微小的翅膀每秒拍打高达八十次，发出柔和的嗡嗡声。它们悬停在半空中，从彩色的花朵中饮用甜美花蜜。

questions.q: What makes hummingbirds unique among birds?
options: They are the smallest birds in the world

questions.q: How fast do a hummingbird's wings beat per second?
What do hummingbirds drink from flowers?

text.en: Recycling paper helps protect forests and save valuable natural trees. Used notebooks and newspapers are taken to a factory, shredded, and mixed with water to make new clean paper sheets.
text.zh: 回收纸张有助于保护森林和节约宝贵的天然树木。用过的笔记本和报纸被送到工厂，碎，并与水混合，制成崭新的干净纸页。

questions.q: Why is recycling paper beneficial for the environment?
options: It helps protect forests and save natural trees

questions.q: What items are taken to the factory for recycling?
What is shredded paper mixed with to form new paper?

text.en: Red foxes have bushy reddish fur, pointed ears, and a long fluffy tail with a white tip. They use their keen sense of hearing to hunt small mice under deep winter snow.
text.zh: 红狐有着浓密的红褐色毛发、尖尖的耳朵和一条带有白尖的漫长蓬松尾巴。它们利用敏锐的听觉在冬天深雪下猎食小老鼠。

questions.q: What color tip does a red fox's fluffy tail have?
What sense does the red fox rely on to hunt under snow?
What prey does the red fox hunt under winter snow?

text.en: The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite. In 1969, astronaut Neil Armstrong became the first human to walk on the Moon's dusty surface. The Moon has no air or liquid water.
text.zh: 月球是地球唯一的天然卫星。1969年，宇航员尼尔·阿姆斯特朗成为第一个在月球满尘表面上步行的咸人类。月球上没有空气或液体水。

questions.q: What is the Moon to planet Earth?
Who was the first human to walk on the Moon in 1969?
What is missing on the Moon's surface?

text.en: Honey is a natural food made by bees that never spoils. Scientists have found jars of honey inside ancient Egyptian tombs that are thousands of years old and still safe to eat.
text.zh: 蜂蜜是由蜜蜂制作的天然食物，永不变质。科学家们在几千年前的古埃及墓穴中发现了装有蜂蜜的罐子，至今仍可安全食用。

questions.q: What special quality does natural honey possess?
Where did scientists find thousands-of-years-old honey jars?
Who creates natural honey?

text.en: Clara and her older brother hiked up a steep rocky trail in the Rocky Mountains. They carried light backpacks containing drinking water and energy bars. At the summit, they saw a grand view.
text.zh: 克拉拉和哥哥沿着洛杉矶山脉一条陡峭的岩石小径徒步登高。他们背着装有饮用水和能量棒的轻便背包。在顶峰，他们看到了壮观的景色。

questions.q: Where did Clara and her brother hike?
options: Up a trail in the Rocky Mountains

questions.q: What supplies were in their backpacks?
What did they see when they reached the summit?

text.en: Frogs go through a process called metamorphosis. They start life as tiny eggs laid in water. Eggs hatch into swimming tadpoles with long tails before growing legs to become adult frogs.
text.zh: 青蛙经历一个被称为变态发育的过程。它们从产在水里的微小卵开始生命。卵孵化成带有长尾巴的游水蝌蚪，然后长出腿变成成体青蛙。

questions.q: What is the transformation process of a frog called?
Where do mother frogs lay their tiny eggs?
What do frog eggs hatch into before growing legs?

text.en: Julian practices playing the violin for twenty minutes every afternoon. He draws a wooden bow across four steel strings to produce sweet musical notes. Julian hopes to play in the school orchestra.
text.zh: 朱利安每天下午练习拉二十分钟小提琴。他用木弓拉过四根钢弦，产生甜美的乐音。朱利安希望能在学校管弦乐队里演奏。

questions.q: How long does Julian practice violin each afternoon?
How many steel strings does a violin have?
What is Julian's musical goal?
options: To play in the school orchestra

text.en: Camels are well adapted to survive in hot dry deserts. They store energy-rich fat in their back humps, allowing them to travel for days without eating food or drinking water.
text.zh: 骆驼非常适应在炎热干燥的沙漠中生存。它们在后背驼峰里储存能量丰富的脂肪，使它们可以在不进食或饮水的情况下行走到数天。

questions.q: What habitat are camels well adapted to live in?
What do camels store inside their back humps?
How does fat in humps help camels travel?
options: Allows them to travel for days without food or water

text.en: On Friday night, Maya made personal pizzas with her family. She spread tomato sauce on flat wheat dough, sprinkled shredded mozzarella cheese, and added sliced mushrooms before baking in a hot oven.
text.zh: 周五晚上，玛雅和家人一起制作了个人比萨。她在平坦的小麦面团上抹上番茄酱，撒上切碎的马苏里拉奶酪，并在放入热烤箱烘烤前加入了切片的蘑菇。

questions.q: When did Maya make pizzas with her family?
What spread did Maya put on the wheat dough first?
What topping ingredients were added before baking?

text.en: Polar bears live on the frozen sea ice of the Arctic Circle. Their thick white fur camouflage blends into the snow, and a thick layer of body blubber keeps them warm in freezing water.
text.zh: 北极熊生活在北极圈结冰的海冰上。它们厚厚的白色毛发伪装融入雪地，一层厚厚的体内脂肪在冰水中保持温暖。

questions.q: Where is the natural habitat of polar bears?
options: Frozen sea ice of the Arctic Circle

questions.q: How does their white fur help polar bears?
options: Camouflage that blends into the snow

questions.q: What body feature keeps polar bears warm in freezing water?
options: A thick layer of body blubber

text.en: Ravens are highly intelligent black birds known for solving complex puzzles. In laboratory tests, ravens can drop pebbles into a narrow water tube to raise the water level and reach a floating treat.
text.zh: 渡鸦是高度聪明的黑鸟，以解决复杂的谜题而闻名。在实验室测试中，渡鸦可以将小石子掉进狭窄的水管里以提高水面，获得悬浮的奖赏食物。

questions.q: What color are ravens?
What ability makes ravens famous among scientists?
How do ravens raise the water level in a narrow tube?
options: By dropping pebbles into the tube

text.en: On clear dark nights, stargazers look up to spot constellations, which are imaginary patterns formed by bright stars. The Big Dipper is a famous constellation shaped like a long-handled water ladle.
text.zh: 在晴朗黑暗的夜晚，观星者抬头寻找星座，这是由明亮的星星构成的想象中的图形。北斗七星是一个著名的星座，形状像一个长柄水勺。

questions.q: What are constellations in the night sky?
options: Imaginary patterns formed by bright stars

questions.q: What famous pattern shape does the Big Dipper resemble?
When is the best time to view constellations?

text.en: Ants live in highly organized colonies with thousands of members. Worker ants search for food, guard the nest, and communicate with each other by leaving invisible chemical scent trails on the ground.
text.zh: 蚂蚁生活在包含数千个成员的高度有组织的群体中。工蚁寻找食物，保卫巢穴，并通过在地面上留下无形的化学气味轨迹相互交流。

questions.q: How are ant colonies structured?
options: Highly organized colonies with thousands of members

questions.q: What duties do worker ants perform?
options: Search for food and guard the nest

questions.q: How do ants communicate paths on the ground?

text.en: Leo went to the dental clinic for his annual checkup. Dr. Evans examined Leo's teeth with a small round mirror and cleaned them with a gentle mint toothpaste. Leo received a blue toothbrush.
text.zh: 里奥去了牙科诊所进行年度检查。埃文斯医生用一把小圆镜检查了里奥的牙齿，并用温和的薄荷牙膏清洗了它们。里奥得到了一把蓝色的新牙刷。

questions.q: Why did Leo visit Dr. Evans?
What tool did Dr. Evans use to examine Leo's teeth?
What gift did Leo receive at the end of the visit?

text.en: A tall white lighthouse stands on a rocky cliff above the ocean waves. Its powerful rotating light beam shines through thick night fog, guiding ships safely away from dangerous hidden rocks.
text.zh: 一座高大的白灯塔耸立在海浪之上的岩石悬崖上。它强大的旋转光束照亮浓浓的夜雾，引导船只安全远离危险的隐蔽岩石。

questions.q: Where is the tall white lighthouse built?
options: On a rocky cliff above ocean waves

questions.q: What does the rotating light beam do in thick fog?
options: Guiding ships safely away from dangerous hidden rocks

questions.q: What color is the lighthouse tower?

text.en: On Arbor Day, Sam and his classmates planted a young oak sapling in the school yard. They dug a deep hole, placed the roots gently inside, and packed fertile soil around the stem before watering.
text.zh: 植树节那天，萨姆和同学们在校园里种下了一株幼小的橡树苗。他们挖了一个深坑，把根部轻轻放入其中，在填水前在茎周围填满肥沃的土壤。

questions.q: What event took place on Arbor Day?
options: Planting a young oak sapling in the school yard

questions.q: What type of tree sapling did Sam plant?
What was the final step after packing fertile soil?

text.en: Eight major planets orbit around the massive hot Sun at the center of our solar system. Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun, while Jupiter is the largest gas giant planet of all.
text.zh: 八大行星围绕我们太阳系中心巨大的热太阳运行。水星是距离太阳最近的行星，而木星是其中最大的气体巨星。

questions.q: How many major planets orbit the Sun?
Which planet is closest to the Sun?
Which planet is the largest in the solar system?

text.en: Sea otters live in cool coastal kelp forests. They float on their backs in ocean water, using flat stones balanced on their bellies to crack open hard shellfish for a tasty lunch.
text.zh: 海獭生活在凉爽的海岸海藻林里。它们在海水中仰泳，利用平衡在肚皮上的平石头砸开坚硬的贝类，享用美味的午餐。

questions.q: Where do sea otters live?
How do sea otters float while eating?
What tool do sea otters use to crack open hard shellfish?
options: Flat stones balanced on their bellies

text.en: Emma helped her grandfather bake a fresh apple pie. They sliced crisp green apples, tossed them with brown sugar and cinnamon, and wrapped them in a golden flaky pie crust.
text.zh: 艾玛帮助爷爷烘烤新鲜的苹果派。他们把脆绿的苹果切片，加入红糖和肉桂粉翻拌，然后裹在金黄酥脆的派皮里。

questions.q: Who baked an apple pie with Emma?
What spices were tossed with the green apple slices?
What wrapped the sweet apple filling?

text.en: Monarch butterflies undergo a complete transformation called metamorphosis during their life cycle. A female butterfly lays a tiny pale egg on the leaf of a milkweed plant. A striped caterpillar hatches and eats milkweed leaves constantly for two weeks. Next, the caterpillar forms a smooth green chrysalis. Inside, it transforms into an adult orange-and-black butterfly.
text.zh: 黑脉金斑蝶在它们的生命周期中经历了被称为完全变态的彻底转变。雌蝶在乳草植物的叶子上产下一个微小的苍白蛋。一条带有条纹的毛毛虫孵化出来，并连续两周不断吃乳草叶子。接下来，毛毛虫形成一个光滑的绿蛹。在内部，它转化为一只黑橙相间的成体蝴蝶。

questions.q: On which specific plant does a female monarch butterfly lay her egg?
What hatches from the butterfly egg?
What smooth protective shell does the caterpillar form?
What colors are the wings of an adult monarch butterfly?

text.en: Thousands of years ago, ancient rulers enjoyed frozen treats made by mixing mountain snow with sweet fruit juices and honey. In the 17th century, Italian chefs developed creamier recipes by churning fresh milk, sugar, and ice together. The modern ice cream cone was popularized at the 1904 World's Fair in St. Louis when a waffle vendor rolled hot waffles into cones to hold ice cream scoop balls.
text.zh: 几千年前，古代统治者享用将高山积雪与甜果汁和蜂蜜混合制成的冷冻甜品。在17世纪，意大利厨师通过将鲜牛奶、糖和冰一起搅拌开发出了更细腻的食谱。现代冰淇淋蛋筒在1904年圣路易斯世博会上得以普及，当时一位华夫饼摊贩将热华夫饼卷成蛋筒来盛放冰淇淋球。

questions.q: What ingredients did ancient rulers mix with mountain snow?
In which century did Italian chefs create creamier milk-based recipes?
Where was the modern ice cream cone popularized in 1904?
What pastry item was rolled into cones to hold ice cream scoops?

text.en: Tropical rainforests are structured in four unique layers, with the canopy layer being the richest in wildlife. The canopy is formed by overlapping tree branches roughly one hundred feet above the ground. Bright toucans, playful spider monkeys, and colorful tree frogs live their whole lives high up in the sunny canopy without ever touching the forest floor.
text.zh: 热带雨林分为四个独特的层次，其中树冠层包含最丰富的野生动物。树冠由离地面大约一百英尺高重叠的树枝组成。鲜艳的巨嘴鸟、活泼的蜘蛛猴和彩色的树蛙一生都生活在阳光明媚的高高树冠层里，从不触及森林地面。

questions.q: How many layers do tropical rainforests have?
How high above the ground is the rainforest canopy layer?
Which bird lives high up in the sunny canopy?
What animal spends its life in the canopy without touching the ground?

text.en: Before paper money existed, people traded heavy metal coins made of gold, silver, and copper. During the Song Dynasty in China, merchants found carrying thousands of heavy iron coins inconvenient for long business trips. They began depositing coins at official stores in exchange for paper receipts called Jiaozi. This marked the birth of the world's first paper currency.
text.zh: 在纸币存在之前，人们交易由金、银、铜制成的重金属硬币。在中国宋朝时期，商人发现携带数千枚沉重的铁钱长途出差非常不便。他们开始将硬币存放在官方店铺中，换取被称为交子的纸质收据。这标志着世界上最早的纸币的诞生。

questions.q: What kind of money did people use before paper money was created?
options: Heavy metal coins made of gold, silver, and copper

questions.q: During which Chinese dynasty was the first paper money introduced?
Why did merchants prefer paper receipts over iron coins?
options: Carrying heavy iron coins was inconvenient

questions.q: What was the name of the first paper currency receipt in Song Dynasty?

text.en: Coral reefs look like underwater rocks, but they are built by tiny soft animals called coral polyps. These polyps absorb calcium from ocean water to build hard stony skeletons around themselves. Over hundreds of years, millions of polyps grow on top of old skeletons, building giant reefs that provide homes for sea turtles, clownfish, and reef sharks.
text.zh: 珊瑚礁看起来像水下岩石，但它们是由被称为珊瑚虫的微小软体动物建造的。这些珊瑚虫从海水中吸收钙，在自身周围建造坚硬的石质骨骼。数百年来，数以百万计的珊瑚虫在旧骨骼之上生长，建造出大型珊瑚礁，为海龟、小丑鱼和礁鲨提供家园。

questions.q: What living creatures build coral reefs?
options: Tiny soft animals called coral polyps

questions.q: What mineral do polyps absorb from sea water to build skeletons?
Where do new coral polyps grow over time?
options: On top of old stony skeletons

questions.q: Name one animal species that finds shelter in coral reefs.

text.en: In 1876, Scottish inventor Alexander Graham Bell made the first successful telephone call. He spoke through a transmitter wire to his assistant in another room, saying: 'Mr. Watson, come here, I want to see you.' This landmark invention allowed human voices to travel long distances through electrical wires for the first time.
text.zh: 1876年，苏格兰发明家亚历山大·格雷厄姆·贝尔成功进行了第一次电话通线。他通过发报电线对另一间房里的助手说：“沃森先生，过来，我想见你。”这一划时代的发明首次使人类的声音能够通过电线长途传播。

questions.q: Who invented the first successful telephone in 1876?
Who was Bell's assistant on the receiving end of the call?
What were the famous first words spoken on the telephone?
options: Mr. Watson, come here, I want to see you

questions.q: How did voices travel in Bell's early telephone system?

text.en: Located off the northeastern coast of Australia, the Great Barrier Reef is the largest living structure on Earth. It is so vast that it can be seen by astronauts from outer space! Thousands of marine species, including green sea turtles, giant clams, and bright blue starfish, thrive in its warm tropical waters.
text.zh: 大堡礁位于澳大利亚东北海岸附近，是地球上最大的活体结构。它如此巨大，以至于宇航员从外太空都能看到它！数以千计的海洋物种，包括绿海龟、巨砗磲和亮蓝海星，在温暖的热带水域中繁衍。

questions.q: Where is the Great Barrier Reef located?
options: Off the northeastern coast of Australia

questions.q: What makes the Great Barrier Reef extraordinary in size?
options: It can be seen by astronauts from space

questions.q: Name a sea creature mentioned that lives in the reef.
What type of water surrounds the Great Barrier Reef?

text.en: Salmon are remarkable fish that spend their adult lives in the ocean but return to the exact freshwater stream where they hatched to lay eggs. During their upstream journey, salmon leap over tall waterfalls and battle strong river currents. Guided by a keen sense of smell, they travel hundreds of miles back home.
text.zh: 鲑鱼是了不起的鱼类，成年后生活在海洋中，但会回到它们孵化的确切淡水小溪产卵。在逆流而上的旅途中，鲑鱼越过高瀑布，与强劲的河水较量。在敏锐嗅觉的指引下，它们游行几百英里回到家园。

questions.q: Where do adult salmon spend most of their grown lives?
Where do salmon return to lay their eggs?
options: To the exact stream where they hatched

questions.q: What obstacle do salmon jump over during their upstream journey?
What sense guides salmon back to their original freshwater birthplace?

title.zh: 太阳能电池板工作原理

text.en: Solar panels convert energy from sunlight into clean electricity for homes and schools. Each panel contains dark silicon solar cells that absorb light particles called photons. When photons hit the cells, they knock electrons free, creating a steady flow of electrical current without producing air pollution.
text.zh: 太阳能电池板将来自阳光的能量转化为供家庭和学校使用的干净电力。每块电池板都包含暗色硅太阳能电池，吸收被称为光子的光粒子。当光子撞击电池时，它们打散自由电子，产生稳定的电流流动，而不产生空气污染。

questions.q: What do solar panels convert sunlight into?
What material are solar cells made of?
What light particles do solar cells absorb?
Why is solar energy environmentally friendly?

text.en: Chocolate was first created over three thousand years ago by ancient Mesoamerican civilizations like the Mayans. They ground roasted cacao beans into a bitter spicy liquid drink used in special ceremonies. Later, European sugar makers added milk and sugar to transform chocolate into the sweet solid treats we enjoy today.
text.zh: 巧克力最早于三千多年前由玛雅人等古代美洲文明所创造。他们将烘烤过的可可豆磨碎成用于特别仪式的苦辣液体饮料。后来，欧洲糖商加入牛奶和糖，将巧克力转化为我们今天享用的甜固态美食。

questions.q: Which ancient civilization first created chocolate drinks?
What ingredient was roasted and ground to make early chocolate drinks?
How did early Mayan chocolate taste?
What ingredients did Europeans add to make chocolate sweet?

text.en: Emperor penguins are the largest of all penguin species, living in the icy freezing continent of Antarctica. During winter, female penguins lay a single egg and travel to the sea to feed. Male penguins balance the egg on their feet under a warm flap of skin for two cold months until it hatches.
text.zh: 帝企鹅是所有企鹅物种中最大的，生活在南极洲冰天雪地的陆地上。冬季期间，母企鹅产下一个蛋并前往大海捕食。公企鹅把蛋平衡在脚上，盖在温暖的皮肤褶皱下两个寒月的时光，直到孵化。

questions.q: Where do emperor penguins live?
How many eggs does a female emperor penguin lay in winter?
Who keeps the egg warm while the female goes to the ocean?
Where is the egg held to stay warm?
options: On feet under a warm flap of skin

text.en: In 1040, a Chinese artisan named Bi Sheng invented movable clay type for printing books. Later in the 1440s, German goldsmith Johannes Gutenberg created a metal printing press with movable lead letters. This revolution enabled fast production of books, allowing knowledge and ideas to spread quickly worldwide.
text.zh: 1040年，一位名叫毕昇的中国工匠发明了用于印刷书籍的活字泥版。后来在15世纪40年代，德国金匠约翰内斯·谷登堡发明了带有可移动铅字的金属印刷机。这一革命实现了书籍的快速生产，使知识和思想在世界范围内快速传播。

questions.q: Who invented movable clay type printing in 1040?
What material did Johannes Gutenberg use for his printing press letters?
In which century did Gutenberg create his metal printing press?
Why was the printing press a revolutionary invention?
options: Allowed fast production of books and spread knowledge

text.en: Chameleons are unique lizards famous for their ability to change skin color. Special skin cells containing tiny color pigments expand or contract based on temperature, mood, and sunlight. Color changes help chameleons communicate with other lizards and camouflage against predators in tree leaves.
text.zh: 变色龙是独特的蜥蜴，以改变皮肤颜色的能力而闻名。包含微小色素的特殊皮肤细胞根据温度、情绪和阳光扩展或收缩。颜色变化有助于变色龙与其他蜥蜴交流，并在树叶中伪装避开捕食者。

questions.q: What special ability makes chameleons famous?
What inside chameleon skin cells causes color changes?
Which factors influence a chameleon's skin color change?
How do color changes benefit chameleons in the wild?
options: Helps communicate and camouflage against predators

text.en: Standing on Liberty Island in New York Harbor, the Statue of Liberty was a gift of friendship from the people of France to the United States in 1886. The giant copper statue holds a flaming torch in her right hand and a tablet dated July 4, 1776, in her left hand.
text.zh: 自由女神像屹立在纽约港的自由岛上，是1886年法国人民送给美国的友谊礼物。这座巨大的铜像右手握着燃烧的火炬，左手拿着刻有1776年7月4日日期的板牌。

questions.q: Which country gifted the Statue of Liberty to the United States?
In what year was the Statue of Liberty dedicated?
What metal is the outer skin of the statue made of?
What date is inscribed on the tablet held in the statue's left hand?

text.en: Owls are nocturnal birds of prey equipped with extraordinary night vision. Their large round eyes cannot turn in their sockets, so owls can rotate their necks up to 270 degrees to look around! Soft fringe feathers on their wings allow them to fly completely silently to catch prey.
text.zh: 猫头鹰是夜行性猛禽，具备非凡的夜视能力。它们圆圆的大眼睛不能在眼窝里转动，所以猫头鹰可以将脖子旋转高达270度来环顾四周！翅膀上柔软的羽毛边缘使它们能完全静音飞行捕捉猎物。

questions.q: What word describes birds like owls that are active at night?
How far can an owl rotate its neck to look around?
Why can't owls roll their eyes inside their sockets?
options: Their large eyes are fixed in place

questions.q: What feather feature allows owls to fly silently?
options: Soft fringe feathers on wing edges

text.en: The Amazon Rainforest in South America is the largest tropical rainforest on planet Earth, spanning across nine different countries. It produces roughly twenty percent of the world's oxygen and is home to one in ten known species on Earth. Giant kapok trees stretch up to two hundred feet into the sky, while mysterious pink river dolphins swim in the winding Amazon River. Thousands of rare plant species growing in the Amazon contain compounds used to create modern lifesaving medicines.
text.zh: 位于南美洲的亚马逊雨林是地球上最大的热带雨林，跨越九个不同的国家。它大约创造了世界百分之二十的氧气，是地球上已知物种中十分之一的家园。巨型的吉贝树高达两百英尺伸入天空，而神秘的粉红河豚在弯曲的亚马逊河中游泳。亚马逊地区生长的数千种稀有植物物种含有用于制造现代救命药物的化合物。

questions.q: On which continent is the Amazon Rainforest located?
Roughly what percentage of the world's oxygen does the Amazon produce?
How tall can giant kapok trees grow in the Amazon?
What unique dolphin species lives in the Amazon River?
Why are Amazonian plant species valuable to medical science?
options: They contain compounds used for modern medicines

text.en: The earliest ancestor of the bicycle was invented in 1817 by German inventor Karl von Drais. Called a running machine, it was made entirely of wood and had no pedals; riders pushed their feet against the ground to move forward. In the 1870s, the High-Wheel bicycle became popular, featuring a giant front wheel and a small rear wheel. Finally, in 1885, John Kemp Starley introduced the Safety Bicycle with equal-sized wheels and a chain drive, creating the design we use today.
text.zh: 自行车最早的祖先于1817年由德国发明家卡尔·冯·德赖斯发明。被称为跑步机，它完全由木头制成，没有脚踏板；骑行者用脚抵住地面向前推进。在19世纪70年代，高轮自行车流行起来，其特点是一个巨型前轮和一个小后轮。最后在1885年，约翰·凯姆普·斯塔利推出了带有等大车轮和链条驱动的安全自行车，创造了我们今天使用的设计。

questions.q: Who invented the wooden running machine in 1817?
How did riders move the 1817 running machine forward?
options: Pushed their feet against the ground

questions.q: What feature characterized the High-Wheel bicycle of the 1870s?
options: Giant front wheel and small rear wheel

questions.q: Who invented the Safety Bicycle in 1885?
What innovation made the Safety Bicycle similar to modern bikes?
options: Equal-sized wheels and a chain drive

text.en: Deep beneath Earth's solid crust, extreme heat melts rock into a thick glowing liquid called magma. Because magma is lighter than surrounding solid rock, it rises slowly through deep cracks in the Earth. When pressure builds up underground, the magma forces its way out through a volcanic vent. Once magma reaches Earth's surface, it is called lava. Volcanic eruptions also release clouds of ash, steam, and poisonous gases into the sky.
text.zh: 在地球坚硬地壳深处，极度的热量将岩石熔化成称为岩浆的浓稠发光液体。因为岩浆比周围的固态岩石轻，它沿着地球深处的缝隙慢慢上升。当地下压力积聚时，岩浆通过火山喷口强行喷出。一旦岩浆到达地球表面，它就被称为熔岩。火山喷发还会向空中释放火山灰、蒸汽和有毒气体云。

questions.q: What is molten rock called when it is deep underground?
Why does magma rise toward the surface of the Earth?
options: It is lighter than surrounding solid rock

questions.q: What is molten rock called after it reaches Earth's surface?
What opening does magma pass through during an eruption?
What else is released into the sky during a volcanic eruption?
options: Clouds of ash, steam, and gases

text.en: The Great Wall of China is a massive series of stone and brick fortifications built across northern China over two thousand years. Construction began during the Qin Dynasty under Emperor Qin Shi Huang to protect the country from invading forces. Watchtowers were built at regular intervals so guards could send smoke signals by day and fire signals by night to warn of danger. Today, millions of tourists visit the Great Wall every year.
text.zh: 中国长城是一系列横跨中国北部的巨型石砖防御工事，历时两千多年建成。建设始于秦朝秦始皇时期，旨在保护国家免受入侵势力的侵害。烽火台定期建设，以便卫兵白天发送烟雾信号，夜晚发送火光信号警示危险。如今，每年有数以百万计的游客参观长城。

questions.q: How long ago did construction of the Great Wall begin?
Which emperor unified and expanded the early Great Wall?
Why was the Great Wall constructed across northern China?
options: To protect the country from invading forces

questions.q: How did guards communicate danger from watchtowers during daytime?
What signal method was used on watchtowers at night?

text.en: Sea turtles are ancient marine reptiles that have swam in the world's oceans for over one hundred million years. Unlike land turtles, sea turtles cannot pull their heads or flippers inside their streamlined shells. Female sea turtles travel thousands of miles to return to the exact beach where they hatched to lay their eggs. They dig holes in warm sand, lay about one hundred eggs, and return to the sea.
text.zh: 海龟是古老的海洋爬行动物，已经在世界海洋中游行了一亿多年。与陆龟不同，海龟不能把头或鳍肢缩进流线型的壳里。母海龟游行数千英里回到它们孵化的确切沙滩产卵。它们在温暖的沙滩上挖坑，产下大约一百个蛋，然后返回大海。

questions.q: For how many years have sea turtles swam in Earth's oceans?
How do sea turtles differ from land turtles regarding their shells?
options: They cannot pull heads or flippers inside shells

questions.q: Where do female sea turtles return to lay their eggs?
options: To the exact beach where they hatched

questions.q: About how many eggs does a female sea turtle lay in her nest?
What shape are sea turtle shells adapted for swimming?

text.en: Earth's outer crust is broken into large puzzle pieces called tectonic plates that float on hot mantle rock. As these giant plates slowly slide past one another, their rough edges often get stuck together. Energy builds up at the stuck boundary until the rock breaks, releasing sudden shockwaves through the ground. Scientists measure earthquake intensity using a sensitive instrument called a seismograph.
text.zh: 地球的外壳分裂成称为板块的大拼图块，在热地幔岩石上漂浮。当这些巨型板块慢慢相互滑动时，它们的粗糙边缘往往卡在一起。能量在卡的边界处积聚，直到岩石断裂，通过地面释放出突然的冲击波。科学家使用被称为地表地震仪的敏感仪器测量地震强度。

questions.q: What are the large pieces of Earth's crust called?
What happens when rough edges of tectonic plates get stuck?
options: Energy builds up until rock breaks

questions.q: What passes through the ground during an earthquake break?
What instrument measures earthquake intensity?
What material do tectonic plates float on?

text.en: Ants are social insects that live in structured underground colonies headed by a queen ant. Worker ants gather food, care for young larvae, and defend the nest from enemy insects. Ants communicate through chemical scent signals called pheromones. When a worker ant finds a sweet food source, it leaves a pheromone trail on the ground so other ants can follow the path easily.
text.zh: 蚂蚁是社群性昆虫，生活在由蚁后领导的有组织的地下群体中。工蚁收集食物，照料幼小的幼虫，并保卫巢穴免受敌害昆虫的侵犯。蚂蚁通过称为信息素的化学气味信号交流。当工蚁找到甜食物源时，它会在地面上留下信息素轨迹，以便其他蚂蚁能轻松跟随路径。

questions.q: Who heads the structured colony in an ant nest?
What duties do worker ants perform in the colony?
options: Gather food, care for larvae, and defend nest

questions.q: What chemical scent signals do ants use to communicate?
Why does a worker ant leave a pheromone trail on the ground?
options: So other ants can follow the food path easily

questions.q: What are young baby ants called inside the nest?

text.en: For centuries, humans dreamed of flying like birds through the sky. In 1903, American brothers Orville and Wilbur Wright built the first successful powered airplane in Kitty Hawk, North Carolina. Their wooden aircraft, called the Wright Flyer, flew for twelve seconds and traveled 120 feet. This historic flight launched the modern age of aviation and space travel.
text.zh: 几个世纪以来，人类梦想着像鸟儿一样在空中飞行。1903年，美国莱特兄弟奥维尔和威尔伯在北卡罗来纳州基蒂霍克建造了第一架成功的动力飞机。他们的木制飞机被称为莱特飞行者号，飞行了12秒，飞行距离为120英尺。这次历史性的飞行开创了现代航空和太空飞行的新时代。

questions.q: Who built the first successful powered airplane in 1903?
Where did the historic first flight take place?
What was the name of the Wright brothers' first aircraft?
How long did the first powered flight last in seconds?
How many feet did the Wright Flyer travel on its first flight?

text.en: Getting enough quality sleep is essential for growing children to stay healthy and alert. During deep sleep, the brain processes memories from the day, and the body releases growth hormones to repair muscles and tissues. Children aged 8 to 12 need about 9 to 11 hours of sleep each night. Lack of sleep can cause poor concentration, moodiness, and weakened immunity.
text.zh: 获得足够的优质睡眠对于成长中的儿童保持健康和警觉至关重要。在深度睡眠期间，大脑处理一天的记忆，身体释放生长激素来修复肌肉和组织。8至12岁的儿童每晚需要大约9至11个小时的睡眠。缺乏睡眠会导致注意力不集中、情绪化和免疫力下降。

questions.q: What process does the brain perform during deep sleep?
What hormone is released by the body during deep sleep?
options: Growth hormones to repair muscles and tissues

questions.q: How many hours of sleep do children aged 8 to 12 need per night?
What is one negative effect of lack of sleep in children?
Why is sleep vital for physical growth?
options: Releases growth hormones for muscle repair

text.en: Deserts are dry biomes that receive less than ten inches of rainfall per year. Plants and animals living in deserts have unique adaptations to conserve water. Cacti store rainwater in thick fleshy stems and use sharp spines to protect against thirsty animals. Nocturnal animals like kangaroo rats stay underground in cool burrows during hot days and hunt at night.
text.zh: 沙漠是每年降雨量少于十英寸的干燥生物群落。生活在沙漠中的植物和动物有着独特的适应机制来节约水分。仙人掌在厚厚的肉质茎中储存雨水，并用尖刺抵抗口渴的动物。像跳鼠这样的夜行性动物在炎热的白天待在凉爽的地下洞穴中，在夜间猎食。

questions.q: How much rainfall do desert biomes receive annually?
Where do cacti store absorbed rainwater?
What feature protects cacti from thirsty animals?
How do kangaroo rats avoid extreme daytime desert heat?
When do nocturnal desert animals come out to hunt?

text.en: As human populations expand worldwide, global demand for clean energy continues to rise rapidly. Traditional energy sources like coal, oil, and natural gas are fossil fuels formed millions of years ago from ancient plant and animal remains. Burning fossil fuels releases harmful carbon emissions into the atmosphere, contributing to global climate change. In response, scientists and engineers are developing renewable energy sources that never run out and produce zero pollution. Solar power uses photovoltaic panels to convert radiant sunlight directly into electric current. Wind power uses giant mechanical wind turbines with massive spinning blades to generate clean electricity from atmospheric air currents. Hydroelectric power harnesses the energy of rushing river water passing through giant dams to turn electric turbines. By transitioning to renewable energy, humanity can build a cleaner, sustainable future for generations to come.
text.zh: 随着全球人口增加，全球对清洁能源的需求持续迅速上升。煤炭、石油和天然气等传统能源是数百万年前由古代动植物遗骸形成的化石燃料。燃烧化石燃料向大气中释放有害碳排放，加剧了全球气候变化。对此，科学家和工程师们正在开发永不枯竭且零污染的可再生能源。太阳能利用光伏电池板将辐射阳光直接转化为电流。风能利用带有巨大旋转叶片的巨型机械风力发电机从大气气流中产生清洁电力。水力发电利用穿过大型水坝的急流河水能量来转动发电机。通过向可再生能源过渡，人类可以为子孙后代建设一个更清洁、可持续的未来。

questions.q: Why are coal, oil, and natural gas classified as fossil fuels?
options: Formed millions of years ago from ancient plant and animal remains

questions.q: What negative impact does burning fossil fuels have on Earth?
options: Releases harmful carbon emissions into the atmosphere

questions.q: What is a major advantage of renewable energy sources?
options: They never run out and produce zero pollution

questions.q: What technology converts sunlight directly into electric current?
How do wind turbines generate clean electrical power?
options: Using massive spinning blades turned by air currents

questions.q: What natural force does hydroelectric power harness to turn turbines?
options: Energy of rushing river water passing through dams

title.en: The History of the Olympic Games

text.en: The historic tradition of the Olympic Games originated in ancient Greece over 2,700 years ago in 776 BC. Held in the sacred valley of Olympia every four years, the ancient games were dedicated to Zeus, the king of the Greek gods. Athletes from different city-states traveled to compete in foot races, wrestling, javelin throw, and chariot racing. During the games, a sacred truce was declared across Greece, stopping all wars so athletes and spectators could travel safely. Winners were awarded crowns woven from wild olive leaves, bringing great honor to their home cities. The ancient games ended in 393 AD but were revived as the modern Olympic Games in Athens in 1896 by French educator Baron Pierre de Coubertin. Today, thousands of international athletes compete in the Summer and Winter Olympic Games every four years, promoting international peace and sporting excellence.
text.zh: 奥运会的历史传统源于公元前776年2700多年前的古希腊。古奥运会每四年在圣地奥林匹亚山谷举行一次，献给希腊众神之王宙斯。来自不同城邦的运动员前往参加赛跑、摔跤、标枪投掷和战车比赛。在比赛期间，希腊全境宣布神圣停战，停止所有战争，以便运动员和观众安全出行。获胜者被授予用野橄榄叶编织的皇冠，为他们的家乡城邦带来巨大的荣誉。古代奥运会于公元393年结束，但由法国教育家皮埃尔·德·顾拜旦男爵于1896年在雅典作为现代奥运会复兴。如今，数以千计的国际运动员每四年参加夏季和冬季奥运会，促进国际和平与体育卓越。

questions.q: Where and when did the ancient Olympic Games originate?
options: Ancient Greece in 776 BC at Olympia

questions.q: Which Greek god were the ancient Olympic Games dedicated to?
What special rule was declared across Greece during the ancient games?
options: A sacred truce stopping all wars

questions.q: What reward did ancient Olympic winners receive?
options: Crowns woven from wild olive leaves

questions.q: Who revived the modern Olympic Games in Athens in 1896?
How often are the modern Summer and Winter Olympic Games celebrated?

text.en: Photosynthesis is the fundamental biological process that allows green plants, algae, and some bacteria to transform solar light energy into chemical energy. Leaves are the primary site of photosynthesis in plants. Inside specialized plant leaf cells, microscopic green organelles called chloroplasts absorb sunlight using a pigment named chlorophyll. The plant absorbs carbon dioxide gas from atmospheric air through tiny leaf pores called stomata and draws up fresh water from the soil through its root system. Using light energy, chloroplasts break apart water molecules and combine them with carbon dioxide to manufacture glucose, a rich sugar that nourishes the plant. Photosynthesis also produces oxygen gas as a byproduct, which is released through stomata back into the air. This vital process maintains Earth's oxygen levels and forms the foundation of nearly all ecological food chains.
text.zh: 光合作用是允许绿色植物、藻类和一些细菌将太阳光能转化为化学能的基本生物学过程。叶片是植物进行光合作用的主要场所。在专门的植物叶片细胞内部，被称为叶绿体的微观绿色细胞器利用名为叶绿素的色素吸收阳光。植物通过被称为气孔的微小叶孔从大气中吸收二氧化碳气体，并从土壤中通过根系吸取新鲜水分。利用光能，叶绿体打散水分子，将其与二氧化碳结合制成葡萄糖，这是一种滋养植物的丰富糖分。光合作用还产生氧气作为副产品，通过气孔释放回空气中。这一至关重要的过程维持着地球的氧气水平，并构成几乎所有生态食物链的基础。

questions.q: What type of energy do green plants convert into chemical energy during photosynthesis?
